title: Psoralen promotes SOCS5 to inhibit JAK/STAT3 to alleviate cartilage degeneration in knee osteoarthritis.
authors: Zhang, Jiahao; Tian, Jiaqing; Weiyang, Wenxiang; Yang, Yunhong; Li, Yiyan; Ye, Xiangling; Huang, Dane; Xu, Xuemeng
journal: Phytomedicine : international journal of phytotherapy and phytopharmacology
one_liner_zh: 该文研究补骨脂素通过SOCS5抑制JAK/STAT3通路缓解膝骨关节炎软骨退变，仅用分子对接初步涉及蛋白-小分子结合，无蛋白质-DNA互作体系、无AI/物理模拟方法，与本课题无关。
abstract: BACKGROUND: Knee osteoarthritis (KOA) is a prevalent degenerative joint disease characterized by progressive cartilage destruction. Bushen Qiangjin Capsule (BSQJ) is a clinically used traditional medicine for KOA, yet its active ingredients and mechanisms of action remain unclear. PURPOSE: This study aimed to identify the key active ingredient in BSQJ and investigate its therapeutic target and mechanism against KOA. MATERIALS AND METHODS: We integrated bioinformatics analysis of GEO datasets with molecular docking to pinpoint key targets. The therapeutic effects of the identified compound, psoralen, were then validated in a rat model of KOA using micro-CT, gait analysis, and histological staining. The mechanism was further investigated in LPS-induced chondrocytes and via siRNA silencing. RESULTS: Bioinformatics analysis identified 13 upregulated proteins and 12 downregulated proteins in KOA and SOCS5 as a key diagnostic target for KOA. Psoralen, a primary active ingredient in BSQJ, exhibited strong binding to SOCS5. In KOA rats, psoralen treatment significantly improved gait abnormalities, reduced subchondral bone sclerosis, and promoted cartilage repair. In vitro, psoralen reversed the imbalance in extracellular matrix (ECM) synthesis and enhanced chondrocyte proliferation. Mechanistically, psoralen exerted its effects by upregulating SOCS5, thereby downregulating JAK and phosphorylation of STAT3. CONCLUSION: Our findings demonstrate that psoralen is a key therapeutic component of BSQJ for KOA treatment. It alleviates cartilage degeneration by targeting SOCS5 and modulating the JAK-STAT3 pathway, thereby restoring chondrocyte metabolic homeostasis. This study provides a pharmacological basis for psoralen as a promising candidate drug for KOA.
abstract_zh: 背景：膝骨关节炎（KOA）是一种常见的退行性关节疾病，以进行性软骨破坏为特征。补肾强筋胶囊（BSQJ）是临床上用于治疗KOA的传统药物，但其活性成分和作用机制尚不清楚。目的：本研究旨在鉴定BSQJ中的关键活性成分，并探讨其治疗KOA的靶点及机制。材料与方法：我们将GEO数据集的生物信息学分析与分子对接相结合，以确定关键靶点。随后，在KOA大鼠模型中，通过micro-CT、步态分析和组织学染色验证了所鉴定化合物补骨脂素（psoralen）的治疗效果。其机制进一步在LPS诱导的软骨细胞中及通过siRNA沉默进行了研究。结果：生物信息学分析在KOA中鉴定出13个上调蛋白和12个下调蛋白，并将SOCS5确定为KOA的关键诊断靶点。补骨脂素是BSQJ中的主要活性成分，与SOCS5表现出强结合力。在KOA大鼠中，补骨脂素治疗显著改善了步态异常，减少了软骨下骨硬化，并促进了软骨修复。在体外，补骨脂素逆转了细胞外基质（ECM）合成失衡，并增强了软骨细胞增殖。机制上，补骨脂素通过上调SOCS5发挥作用，从而下调JAK及STAT3的磷酸化。结论：我们的研究结果表明，补骨脂素是BSQJ治疗KOA的关键治疗成分。它通过靶向SOCS5并调节JAK-STAT3通路，从而恢复软骨细胞代谢稳态，减轻软骨退变。本研究为补骨脂素作为KOA的候选药物提供了药理学基础。
